event: Fortiche founded in Paris by Jérôme Combe, Pascal Charrue, and Arnaud Delord.
Riot and Fortiche begin their long collaboration around Jinx and Get Jinxed.
Get Jinxed publicly establishes the visual and musical language around Jinx.
Warriors expands Riot and Fortiche’s music-cinematic collaboration.
Seconds develops Ekko through a short, highly graphic cinematic.
Arcane concept development begins inside Riot; early work tests whether a game company can sustain long-form television storytelling.
Early story and visual tests focus on Vi, Jinx/Powder, Piltover, and Zaun.
A production-quality crisis forces substantial rethinking rather than a straight march from pitch to release.
RISE demonstrates another large-scale Fortiche/Riot music-production workflow.
POP/STARS demonstrates Riot’s ability to coordinate music, character performance and global event marketing.
Riot announces Arcane during League of Legends’ ten-year anniversary with a 2020 target.
Riot delays Arcane to 2021 because COVID-19 disrupts international, highly collaborative production.
Enemy music video launches before the series.
Riot announces the global Twitch co-streaming premiere.
Final trailer confirms the November 6 premiere.
RiotX Arcane begins as a month-long ecosystem campaign.
Jinx enters Fortnite, the first League champion in a non-Riot game.
Season One Act I premieres globally on Netflix; Tencent Video carries the series in China.
Season One Act II releases.
Season One Act III releases.
Riot confirms Season Two is already in production.
Riot announces a significant non-controlling equity stake in Fortiche and two Fortiche board seats.
Arcane wins nine Annie Awards.
Bridging the Rift begins releasing its five-part production documentary.
Arcane wins Outstanding Animated Program and three juried individual-achievement Emmys.
Arcane wins Best Adaptation at The Game Awards.
Riot announces that new Runeterra storytelling will operate under one shared canon.
GKIDS acquires global video and transactional rights for home entertainment.
Riot says Arcane’s story had a clear ending and that Season Two would close it; other projects remained early.
Riot separates film and television work into animation and live-action studios.
Season One becomes available to own digitally under the GKIDS rollout.
Season One standard disc editions launch.
Season One collector’s edition launches.
Season Two Act I premieres.
Season Two Act II premieres.
Season Two Act III and the series finale premiere.
Netflix publishes a detailed Season Two production feature describing a three-year effort and roughly 450 artists at peak.
The Art and Making of Arcane is published.
Los Angeles Times publishes a disputed $250 million production-and-marketing estimate and economic analysis.
Autodesk publishes Fortiche’s Season Two crowd-production case study.
Ma Meilleure Ennemie receives a Fortiche-produced standalone music video extending the Ekko/Powder sequence.
Season Two receives Emmys for Animated Program, Sound Editing, Background Design, and Color.
Season Two standard 4K and Blu-ray editions release.
League stages an Arcane finale-anniversary event and returns Arcane skins.
Season Two collector’s edition release date.
Fortiche continues Riot collaboration while reorganizing for multiple projects and original IP development.
Research cutoff: no specific successor Arcane series is treated as officially announced.
